# Security & SVG Sanitization Checklist: ArtCraft Local Authoring

**Purpose**: Requirements-quality review of the SVG content security gate — the reject-list floor, allow-list posture, dangerous vector coverage, DoS hardening, and build-time placement that protects the build host (not just browsers) from malicious or malformed SVG masters.

**Created**: 2026-10-17
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) — FR-002, FR-013, Constitution Principle II

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `__SPECKIT_COMMAND_CHECKLIST__` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

---

## Threat Model & Scope Definition

- [x] CHK001 — Is the threat model for SVG masters explicitly defined, distinguishing build-host risks (SSRF via external refs, XXE/DoS via libxml2) from browser risks (script execution)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK002 — Is the scope of the sanitization gate clearly limited to SVG masters, with explicit exclusion of raster formats (PNG/JPG) from this specific gate? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK003 — Are the asset types subject to the gate (SVG only) versus those subject only to geometry/budget checks (PNG/JPG) explicitly distinguished? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK004 — Is the rationale for why sharp rasterization is explicitly stated as insufficient for sanitization (it protects the encoder, not the host from SSRF/XXE) documented? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002]

## Reject-List Completeness (Minimum Baseline)

- [x] CHK005 — Are `<script>` elements explicitly enumerated in the reject-list? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK006 — Are `on*` event handler attributes (e.g., `onclick`, `onload`, `onerror`) explicitly enumerated in the reject-list? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK007 — Is `foreignObject` explicitly enumerated in the reject-list (it enables HTML namespace injection and script execution)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK008 — Are external `href`/`xlink:href` references (protocol-relative, absolute URL, scheme-based) explicitly enumerated in the reject-list? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK009 — Is the explicit rejection of **all DOCTYPE** declarations (not just entity declarations) specified for XXE/billion-laughs hardening? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK010 — Is the enumerated reject-list explicitly characterized as a **minimum floor, not an exhaustive list**? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002]

## Extended Reject-List (Beyond Minimum Baseline)

- [x] CHK011 — Are CSS-based attack vectors explicitly enumerated: `url()`, `@import`, `image-set()`, `expression()`, `-moz-binding`, `behavior:`? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK012 — Is the preference stated to reject the `<style>` element and `style` attribute entirely for authored masters (rather than attempting CSS sanitization)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK013 — Are all `data:` URIs in any URL-valued attribute explicitly rejected? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK014 — Are SMIL animation elements that mutate `href`/`xlink:href` explicitly enumerated: `animate`, `set`, `animateMotion`, `animateTransform`, `discard`? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK015 — Are dangerous elements that DOMPurify forbids explicitly enumerated: `iframe`, `object`, `embed`, `base`, `meta`, `link`, `form`, `template`, `noscript`, `handler`, `listener`? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK016 — Are `xml:base`, `externalResourcesRequired`, processing instructions, and XInclude explicitly enumerated in the reject-list? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]

## DoS & Resource-Exhaustion Hardening

- [x] CHK017 — Are file-size limits for SVG masters explicitly specified (not just "DoS caps" referenced vaguely)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK018 — Are element-count limits for SVG masters explicitly specified? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK019 — Are nesting-depth limits for SVG masters explicitly specified? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK020 — Are the DoS caps defined as measurable thresholds (e.g., maximum file bytes, maximum element count, maximum nesting depth) rather than qualitative intent? [Measurability, Spec §FR-002]
  - **Resolved (2026-10-17, batch 8)**: Explicit measurable caps now in FR-002 + Assumptions + `data-model.md` + `research.md`: file size ≤ 1 MB (1 048 576 B), element count ≤ 10 000, nesting depth ≤ 100, attributes/element ≤ 256 (violation → throw). Grounded in librsvg `limits.rs` and billion-laughs CVEs (CVE-2026-29074, CVE-2019-20446); the 256 attributes/element cap is a project-chosen measurable value, not a librsvg-derived limit.

## Allow-List Posture (Hybrid Gate)

- [x] CHK021 — Is the hybrid posture (reject-list floor **plus** allow-list over minimal vectorcraft vocabulary) explicitly specified as the chosen approach? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK022 — Is the allow-list characterized as **fail-closed** (reject anything not in the allow-list)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK023 — Is the allow-list vocabulary explicitly tied to the minimal SVG vocabulary emitted by vectorcraft? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK024 — Is the finalization of the allow-list vocabulary explicitly deferred to planning (not left as an open question for implementation)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK025 — Are internal `url(#…)` fragment references explicitly allowed (not rejected by the gate)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]

## Gate Placement & Failure Behavior

- [x] CHK026 — Is the gate placement explicitly specified: **before** `sourceWidth()`/`encodeImage()` in `build-images.mjs`? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013]
- [x] CHK027 — Is the failure behavior explicitly **fail-fast** (throw on violation) rather than warn-only or skip? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK028 — Is it explicitly stated that sharp `failOn: 'error'` + `limitInputPixels` remain as backstops (not replacements for the gate)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK029 — Is it explicitly stated that the gate protects the build host (SSRF, XXE/DoS via libxml2), not only browsers? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002]

## Consistency & Coverage

- [x] CHK030 — Is the reject-list consistent between the spec body (FR-002) and the Assumptions section (no duplicate or conflicting entries)? [Consistency]
- [x] CHK031 — Is the `isSafeLocalReference` rule (used for manifest references) explicitly distinguished from the SVG href/xlink:href rejection rule (different validation, different scope)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002]
  - **Resolved (2026-10-17, batch 9)**: `isSafeLocalReference` is a file-path rule (manifest/sidecar) and does NOT apply to SVG attributes; the SVG gate allows fragment-only `#…` and rejects absolute/protocol-relative/relative-path/`data:`. FR-002 and `data-model.md` corrected.
- [x] CHK032 — Are there SVG attack vectors not covered by the enumerated reject-list or allow-list posture that should be explicitly addressed? [Coverage, Gap]
- [x] CHK033 — Is the relationship between this gate and the existing safe-local-reference / external-origin checks in `build.mjs` explicitly defined (complementary, not overlapping)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002]
